## Professional Summary

UW-Madison M.S. candidate in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior (expected Dec 2026); B.S. in Psychology (neuroscience concentration, minor in sociology), UW-Parkside. Applied AI practitioner building full-lifecycle systems spanning multi-agent document-intelligence pipelines, transformer fine-tuning and calibration, LLM evaluation, computer vision classification, and behavioral prediction models. Master's capstone with American Family Insurance acting as industry partner, targeting methods to decrease costs of AI inference & improve document intelligence workflows. I bring five years of high-volume logistical & systems operations experience in quality assurance, documentation, and iterative process improvement.

## Projects

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Digital-Mailroom** [DSHB Capstone project — American Family Insurance (industry partner)]{.sub}
:::

- A capstone project with American Family Insurance targeting document intelligence and processing improvements; 10 Python packages, including entity extraction, classification, routing, and scalable workflows, to improve document intelligence and management efficiency.
- Designed and implemented a unified LangGraph pipeline integrating legal-document routing, prompt experimentation, deterministic scoring, dataset management, and deployment workflows in a reproducible Docker environment.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Mailroom-ML** [ML Training, Evaluation & Fine-Tuning]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a ModernBERT document classifier with end-to-end training, evaluation, and fine-tuning pipelines; data lineage tracking, probability calibration, and production routing logic included.
- Implemented PyTorch training pipelines with Transformers and Hugging Face datasets, scipy-based evaluation, and ONNX export for FastAPI serving on Modal; maintained pytest coverage throughout.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**RVL-CDIP-Classifier** [Computer Vision & Prompt Engineering]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a Python toolkit that converts TIFF/PDF pages to 300-DPI images, runs OCR, and classifies documents into 16 RVL-CDIP categories with OpenRouter vision models.
- Ran 17+ prompt iterations and generated confusion matrices, misclassification analyses, and cost projections to guide evidence-based prompt engineering and model selection.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Psychometric Digital Twin** [Behavioral ML Research | UW–Madison]{.sub}
:::

- Built a behavioral prediction pipeline on 252 matched survey participants: traditional ML models (Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP) predicting communication-apprehension scores from demographic, employment, geographic, and transit features, with cross-validation and SHAP feature importance.
- Validated the PRCA's psychometric structure with factor analysis, then built LLM "digital twin" personas via tiered embodiment prompts (OpenRouter/vLLM) and benchmarked them against the ML baselines on shared metrics (MAE, band accuracy, F1), analyzing systematic bias by demographic group.
:::
